title: The Twins' Death and Return
subtitle: A staged death outwits Xibalba's rulers

learningObjectives.text: What happens to the twins' bones after their deaths?
What do the twins do when Xibalba's rulers ask to be revived?

return.excerpt: they stretched themselves upon a funeral pile and died together. Their bones were beaten to powder and thrown into the river, where they sank, and were transformed into young men.
return.note: Verbatim prose from Spence's 1908 English summary, which he says draws on Brasseur de Bourbourg's French and Ximénez's Spanish translations. This is not a direct translation of the K'iche' text.

fate.translator: not applicable; Spence authored this English summary

fate.excerpt: The monarchs of Xibalba, anxious to experience the novel sensation of a temporary death, requested to be slain and resuscitated. They were speedily killed, but the brothers refrained from resuscitating their arch-enemies.
fate.note: Verbatim prose from Spence's 1908 English summary, which he says draws on Brasseur de Bourbourg's French and Ximénez's Spanish translations. This is not a direct translation of the K'iche' text.

narrativeBlocks.title: The twins plan a deception
narrativeBlocks.body: After surviving the ordeals, Hun-Ahpu and Xbalanque tell two sorcerers what to do with their bones, then die on a funeral pyre.

narrativeBlocks.title: Bones return to life
narrativeBlocks.body: Quotation from Spence's English summary (whitespace normalized): “they stretched themselves upon a funeral pile and died together. Their bones were beaten to powder and thrown into the river, where they sank, and were transformed into young men.”

narrativeBlocks.title: The rulers ask for the same power
narrativeBlocks.body: The princes of Xibalba ask the twins to kill and revive them. The twins kill them but refuse to bring them back.

narrativeBlocks.title: Do not confuse the different returns
narrativeBlocks.body: Spence's summary says the twins return to life, then later says their father and uncle rise to heaven and become the Sun and Moon. Those are distinct events in his account.

narrativeBlocks.title: Victory ends the rulers' authority
narrativeBlocks.body: After the princes die, the twins forbid them from playing ball and assign them menial tasks in Spence's version.
